claim: The finisher is Storm King's Thunder followed by Chandra's Ignition on your biggest creature. Attack first so firebending adds red mana. With Leyline Tyrant out, that red lasts into main phase 2. Count every Ignition copy against each opponent's life before you commit, and pass on optional taxes like Rhystic Study that would leave you short.
evidence: Game 0012, round 8: the attack gave 2 red from firebending plus 1 kept by Tyrant. That paid for Storm King's Thunder X=3 at end of combat. Chandra's Ignition on a 5-power Laelia then hit each opponent 4 times for 5 and killed Tidus and Esika. The pilot declined to pay the Rhystic tax to keep enough mana.

claim: When you cast Avatar's Wrath, target your best creature so it stays. Afterward, recast your own airbent creatures (Zuko included, if you left him in exile) for {2} each. Your opponents can't cast from exile until your next turn, so the sweep is close to one-sided. Pay for it with leftover firebending mana.
evidence: Game 0012, round 7: the pilot cast Avatar's Wrath from Blazing Crescendo's exile, targeting Laelia. It exiled Esika, Tidus, Wakka, Birds and the other creatures. The same turn it recast Zuko and Leyline Tyrant for {2} each, partly with firebending red kept by Tyrant, and won the next turn.

claim: Don't tap out for a commander recast plus an attack against an opponent who is building toward a mass effect. Keep a creature back or keep a sweeper or cheap interaction live. Once Zuko is on the battlefield, Flawless Maneuver is free and protects the whole board.
evidence: Game 0006, round 7: the pilot recast Zuko using every land and the Treasure, then attacked with Laelia. That left it tapped out and it used Flawless Maneuver in combat. Lathril then cast Kindred Dominance, destroying Zuko, Laelia and Prosper. Boardless, the pilot died the next round to a 38-damage swing. Untimely Malfunction and Delayed Blast Fireball sat unused in hand the whole game.

claim: Foretell Sozin's Comet as soon as you have a spare {2}. Once Zuko and Isshin are both on the battlefield, cast the Comet from exile for {2}{R} before combat, then attack with everything. Isshin doubles every firebending trigger. Pour that pool into Electrodominance with a big X at an opponent you can target, and use its free cast to put a hard-to-cast card like Ozai into play from your hand.
evidence: Game 4. In round 5 (turn 19) the pilot cast Isshin and foretold the Comet off Sol Ring. In round 6 (turn 23) it cast the Comet from exile, which triggered Zuko's counters, and attacked with Zuko, Goliath Daydreamer and Isshin. The doubled firebending made 26 red. Electrodominance with X=22 took Choco from 22 to 0 and cast Ozai for free. Ozai had been stuck in hand all game because the pilot had only one black source.

claim: Ozai turns your unspent mana red instead of letting it empty, and he has flying and indestructible while you hold 6 or more unspent mana. When an opponent aims destroy removal at him, tap lands in response until your pool reaches 6. Keep at least 6 floating between turns.
evidence: Game 3, round 7 (turn 25). Hearthhull cast Putrefy on Ozai while the pilot held 5 mana. The pilot tapped a Mountain in response to reach 6, so Ozai was indestructible and Putrefy did nothing. The auditor then confirmed the firebending mana stays in the pool at end of combat while Ozai is out, which left the pilot with 14 {R}.

claim: Cast Norin the Wary before Zuko, or together with him. Norin exiles himself whenever any player casts a spell or attacks, and he comes back at every end step. That puts a +1/+1 counter on each of your creatures on every player's turn at no cost, so Zuko's firebending grows before he ever attacks.
evidence: Game 2. Norin came down in round 2 (turn 7) and Zuko as a 2/4 in round 3 (turn 11). Norin returned at the end steps of turns 11, 12 and 13, so by round 4 (turn 15) Zuko had 3 counters and firebending 5. The auditor confirmed he was a 6/8 with Embercleave.

claim: On an attack turn, spend the firebending mana in combat. Embercleave costs {1} less for each attacker, so flash it in on Zuko. Keep a {R} from the pool for Redirect Lightning (paying 5 life as its additional cost) so a bounce or removal spell can't stop the swing.
evidence: Game 2, round 4 (turn 15). Zuko and Laelia attacked, and firebending made 5 {R}. Embercleave cost {2}{R}{R}, paid with 4 of it. Miirym answered with Cyclonic Rift on Zuko, and the leftover {R} paid for Redirect Lightning, which moved the Rift onto Yuriko. The auditor upheld that Zuko connected for 12 commander damage.

claim: Foretell Delayed Blast Fireball early. Party Thrasher gives spells cast from exile convoke, so your creatures can pay part of the {4}{R}{R} foretell cost. Cast from exile, the Fireball deals 5 to each opponent and each of their creatures, which makes it a one-sided wipe. After it resolves, opponents have lost life, so Light Up the Stage costs only its {R} spectacle cost that turn.
evidence: Game 1. In round 4 (turn 14) the pilot cast Thrasher and foretold the Fireball. In round 5 (turn 18) it cast the Fireball from exile, tapping Thrasher for convoke. It killed nine creatures across three opponents and took 5 life from each. The pilot then cast Light Up the Stage (chosen from exile with Thrasher) for {R} from Shinka.

claim: When you have free fights, send them at the opponent whose board you've already flagged as able to kill you, not at the player with the most life. Crystal Barricade prevents noncombat damage only to its controller's other creatures, so a fight can still kill the Barricade itself. That also removes its player hexproof.
evidence: Game 4, round 6 (turn 23). The pilot's notes flagged Felothar's Tree of Perdition, which could swap the pilot's 37 life for its 13 toughness. Yet all three Agni Kai casts went at Mr. House, at 36 life, and his Iron Mastiff. On the next turn Felothar used the Tree to drop the pilot to 13, then killed him with Welcoming Vampire and the unblockable Crystal Barricade.

claim: When Fire Lord Zuko is bounced to your hand, recasting him from hand costs only {R}{W}{B}. Commander tax applies only to casts from the command zone. Plan the turn's mana with the correct cost; don't budget 5 for him.
evidence: Game 0031: Summon: Valefor bounced Zuko to hand on turn 17. On turn 18 the pilot wrote 'That covers Zuko (5 with commander tax) or Etali (6), but not both.' On turn 22 it paid tax from hand, tapping Arcane Signet and Shinka, and then had to untap them to fix its own overpayment.

claim: When one card is in hand and another sits in exile with a play window that closes this turn, play the exiled one first unless the hand card is clearly more urgent. The card in hand will still be there next turn; the exiled one is gone forever.
evidence: Game 0031, round 6 (turn 22): Light Up the Stage had exiled Etali, Primal Storm and Dragonskull Summit, playable only until the end of that turn. The pilot spent the turn recasting Zuko and Party Thrasher from hand, which would still have been castable next turn, and noted 'Etali ... I didn't have the mana, so I lost it.'

claim: Cast Norin the Wary on turn 2, before Zuko, and leave him out. Every spell anyone casts exiles him, and he returns at the next end step, which triggers Zuko's counter for your whole team nearly every turn at no cost.
evidence: Game 0032: Norin came down on turn 7 (round 2) and Zuko on turn 11. Norin blinked on turns 11, 12 and 13, so by turn 15 Zuko was 5 power with 3 counters without casting anything from exile. His firebending 5 then paid for a flashed-in Embercleave, and he attacked as a 6/8 double striker for 12.

claim: Foretell Delayed Blast Fireball as soon as you have a spare {2}, then cast it from exile the next turn, letting Party Thrasher's convoke pay part of the {4}{R}{R}. Five damage to every opponent and each of their creatures is this deck's reset button against go-wide boards. Afterwards, Light Up the Stage costs only its {R} spectacle cost.
evidence: Game 0031: Fireball was foretold on turn 14 alongside Thrasher. On turn 18 it was cast from exile with Thrasher tapped for convoke. It killed all of Edgar's vampires, Hancock, O'aka, Kami and Gyre Sage, and hit each opponent for 5. Light Up the Stage followed for {R} off Shinka.

claim: The free cast from Goliath Daydreamer's attack trigger sets X to 0, so a recast Electrodominance deals no damage. It is still a spell cast from exile, which triggers Zuko. Decline the free cast while Zuko is off the battlefield, then take it once he is out, purely for the team-wide counter.
evidence: Game 0033: on turn 10 the pilot declined the free Electrodominance ('X=0 ... keeping it in exile for a later attack with Zuko out'). On turn 14, with Zuko in play, it cast it free for X=0, and Zuko put a counter on every creature. Game 0034, turn 23: the same X=0 recast was used again for a Zuko trigger.

claim: On the Comet turn, cast the foretold Sozin's Comet for {2}{R} before combat with Zuko and Isshin out, and attack with everything. Isshin doubles each firebending trigger. Then pour the pool into Electrodominance at an opponent you can kill outright, and use its free cast for Ozai so the leftover mana stays in your pool.
evidence: Game 0034, round 6 (turn 23): the Comet was foretold on turn 19 with Sol Ring mana and cast from exile on turn 23. Three attackers with doubled firebending produced 26 red. Electrodominance at X=22 took Choco from exactly 22 to 0 and cast Ozai for free. Then Last Agni Kai fights killed Mr. House's commander and Iron Mastiff.

claim: When removal targets Zuko during combat, respond by casting any spell you can from exile (for example Great Train Heist with the floating firebending mana). Zuko's counter trigger resolves before he leaves. With Ozai out, answer destroy removal by tapping lands until you have 6 unspent mana, which makes him indestructible.
evidence: Game 0033, turn 22: Terra cast Path to Exile on attacking Zuko. The pilot cast Great Train Heist from exile in response with all three modes, and the team got counters before Zuko left. On turn 25, Hearthhull cast Putrefy on Ozai. The pilot tapped a Mountain to bring the pool to 6, and Ozai survived.

claim: A permanent with a stun counter does not untap in your untap step; one stun counter comes off instead. Once a Saga like Summon: Valefor has stunned your creatures, plan your turn without them: don't declare them as attackers or count them as blockers.
evidence: Game 0031, turn 28: Zuko and Runehorn Hellkite each had 2 stun counters from Summon: Valefor. Hellkite was declared attacking Elspeth anyway with Pip-Boy equipped. The auditor undid the attack and Elspeth came back at 7 loyalty, so the pilot lost both the equip mana and the planeswalker kill.

claim: Cast haste creatures such as Laelia, the Blade Reforged in main phase 1, before you pass priority with an empty stack. Passing on an empty stack moves you to combat, and a Laelia cast after combat loses her attack trigger for the turn: no exiled card and no counter.
evidence: Game 0021 (Kuja pod), round 4 (table turn 13): the pilot cast Talisman of Conviction, then passed by mistake and ended up in combat. It attacked with Zuko alone for 2 and cast Laelia in main 2. Its note: 'I meant to cast Laelia before combat so she could attack, but an extra pass moved me out of main phase 1 too early.' Contrast game 0012, round 3 (turn 11): Laelia went down in main 1, attacked the same turn, exiled Arid Mesa and was played from exile.

claim: When an opponent controls Vorinclex, Monstrous Raider, the single +1/+1 counters from Zuko and Laelia and the quest counters on Firebender Ascension all round down to 0. Stop building toward counters and switch to the damage finish: attack, cast Storm King's Thunder with the firebending mana at end of combat, then cast Chandra's Ignition on your biggest creature in main 2. Keep the red with Leyline Tyrant, and count every copy against each opponent's life before you commit.
evidence: Game 0012: from round 5 (turn 19) Vorinclex halved every Zuko, Laelia and Ascension counter to 0, as the pilot noted. In round 8 (turn 30) it attacked, paid for Storm King's Thunder X=3 with 2 firebending R, 1 R kept by Tyrant, Plains, Swamp and Talisman, then cast Chandra's Ignition on 5-power Laelia. Four Ignitions dealt 20 to each opponent, which killed Tidus (12) and Esika (19) together.

claim: With Avatar Roku out, attack and let his six R plus Zuko's firebending pay for everything during combat. After blocks are declared, flash in Embercleave (1 cheaper per attacker), then spend the rest of the pool on Roku's {R}{R}{R}: +3/+0 on the double-striking Zuko. Plan this for commander damage and a one-turn kill, and leave nothing in the pool, because it empties at end of combat.
evidence: Game 0023, round 5 (turn 19): Zuko and Party Thrasher attacked, making 10 R (6 from Roku, 4 from firebending). Embercleave cost {2}{R}{R} out of the pool, and two Roku pumps made Zuko an 11/7 double striker that knocked out Obeka (13 life). In round 7 (turn 24), four Roku pumps took Zuko to 19 power and he killed Rin and Seri from 17.
